paper.title: Active Exploration via Autoregressive Generation of Missing Data

settings.name_in_paper: Informed bandit with known task distribution p*_tasks (general potential outcomes table)
unmapped: The potential-outcomes table tau (K x T) and prior information Z are drawn from a task distribution p*_tasks known to the learner; arbitrary joint distribution, no stationarity/exchangeability required
Unstructured prior task information Z (e.g. text) observed before play
Regret is against the best fixed action in hindsight on the realized table, averaged over the task distribution (Bayesian)
settings.definition_quote: a bandit task B = (Z, \tau) consists of prior task information Z and a two-dimensional array or ``table'' of potential outcomes ... associates with this a reward R(Y_t) \in [0,1] ... We assume that the bandit task B is sampled i.i.d. from the task distribution

settings.name_in_paper: Informed bandit with approximate sequence model (independence across actions + exchangeability)
unmapped: (Z^(a), Y^(a)_{1:T}) drawn i.i.d. across actions from p*_per-action (Assumption 1) and exchangeable over time (Assumption 2)
Learner does not know p* but uses an approximate sequence model p_hat trained offline; bounds depend on its excess log-loss

conditions: exact posterior samples from the true task distribution

source.label: prop:regret_TS_exact
source.quote: Let $\pi_{\rm TSAR}$ denote Algorithm \ref{alg:Thompson_sampling_generic}. Assume rewards are bounded and normalized so that $R(y)\in [0,1]$ for any outcome $y$. Then, $\Delta(\pi_{\rm TSAR}) \leq \sqrt{\frac{|\Aeval| \log(|\Aeval|)}{2T} }$.

results.notes: Paper bounds per-period regret; multiplied by T. Paper says it is an immediate consequence of Russo & Van Roy (2016) / Bubeck et al.; recorded as the paper's own proposition.

symbols.E_S: expected size of the candidate set E[|S(Z)|], S(Z) = {a: P(A*=a | Z) > 1/T}

source.label: cor:screening
source.quote: Let $\pi_{\rm TSAR}$ denote Algorithm~\ref{alg:Thompson_sampling_generic} applied with exact posterior samples satisfying~\eqref{eq:posterior-sampling-def}. For threshold $\epsilon = 1/T$, \Delta(\pi_{\rm TSAR}) \le \frac{|\cA|-\E[|S(Z)|]}{T} + \sqrt{\frac{\E[|S(Z)|]\cdot\log|\cA|}{2T}}.

results.notes: Per-period bound multiplied by T. Dependence on prior via E[|S(Z)|] (prior-dependent, labelled instance_dependent).

symbols.eps_loss: excess offline log-loss of the sequence model, l(p_hat) - l(p*)

conditions: history generated by an arbitrary policy pi

source.label: prop:posterior_sample
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. If, after employing some policy $\pi$ for $t-1$ time periods, Algorithm \ref{alg:posterior_sample} is applied to the history $\HH_{t-1}$ with sequence model $\widehat{p}_{per-action}$ to generate ... $\E_\pi[ D_{\rm KL}(...)] \leq |\Aeval| [\ell(\widehat{p}) - \ell(p^*)]$.

results.notes: Bound on expected KL between generated and true posterior samples, not a regret bound.

symbols.Delta_sim: per-period regret of policy pi in the simulator induced by p_hat

source.label: prop:sim-to-real-gap

results.notes: Reduction for any policy; per-period bound multiplied by T.

tuning: TSAR run with approximate sequence model p_hat
results.notes: Per-period bound multiplied by T. Example 2 specializes this to a misspecified prior with eps_loss replaced by KL(nu_* || nu_theta); not recorded separately.

conditions: specific algorithm: TSAR with a misspecified Beta... (three-point) prior p_hat
Bernoulli outcomes, eta in {1/4,1/2,3/4}, Z in {Safe, Risky}, misspecified prior puts mass 1/T^2 on 3/4 for Risky arms

source.quote: Therefore, for $|\Aeval|=O(1)$, the per-period regret of misspecified Thompson sampling is bounded below by a positive constant: $\Delta(\psar(\widehat{p}); p^*) \geq \Omega(1)$.

results.notes: Per-period Omega(1) lower bound multiplied by T gives linear cumulative regret; shows T-independence of penalty term is tight. Stated in an Example, informal argument.

cited_results.setting_description: Bayesian bandit, bad-prior regime where rho is the prior mass assigned to the true model
Bayesian K-armed bandit with rewards in [0,1], regret per period (information-theoretic analysis)
